root.label: Overload Resolution
root.note: Every overloaded call passes through candidate lookup, viability filtering, and conversion ranking.

children.label: Three-Phase Pipeline
children.note: Overload resolution constructs candidates, eliminates non-viable matches, and crowns one winner.

children.label: 1. Build candidate set
children.note: Name lookup, ADL, and template argument deduction gather all visible overloads.

children.label: 2. Filter viable functions
children.note: Requires matching arity, satisfied C++20 constraints, and an implicit conversion per argument.

children.label: 3. Pick best viable
children.note: Selects the candidate no worse on every parameter and strictly better on at least one.

children.label: Conversion Sequence Tiers
children.note: Implicit conversion sequences rank across three strict tiers before tie-breakers apply.

children.label: Standard conversion sequence
children.note: Built-in language conversions outrank all user-defined constructors and operators.

children.label: User-defined conversion sequence
children.note: Uses at most one converting constructor or conversion operator between standard conversions.

children.label: Ellipsis conversion sequence
children.note: Matches C-style variadic parameters only when no better conversion exists.

children.label: Standard Sub-Ranks
children.note: Within standard conversions, exact matches beat promotions, which beat conversions.

children.label: Exact match and qualification
children.note: Includes identity, array-to-pointer decay, lvalue-to-rvalue, and adding const qualifiers.

children.label: Promotions preserve value
children.note: Widening char, short, or bool to int and float to double beats general conversions.

children.label: Lossy and pointer conversions
children.note: Includes int-to-double, Derived*-to-Base*, and pointer-to-bool conversions.

children.label: Reference and Qualifier Rules
children.note: Value category and const qualifiers break exact-match ties on references and *this.

children.label: Lvalue prefers T& over const
children.note: A mutable lvalue selects T& over const T& because it requires fewer cv-qualifications.

children.label: Rvalue prefers T&& over const
children.note: Temporaries and xvalues prefer rvalue references T&& over const T&.

children.label: Implicit *this ref-qualifiers
children.note: Member cv and & or && qualifiers participate as the implicit object parameter.

children.label: Tie-Breakers and Traps
children.note: When conversions tie completely, language-level rules settle templates, concepts, and deleted calls.

children.label: Non-template wins equal ties
children.note: Non-template overloads win only after parameter conversion ranks tie completely.

children.label: C++20 constraint subsumption
children.note: More constrained templates beat less constrained templates when conversions tie.

children.label: Deleted and private checked last
children.note: Overload resolution selects = delete or private winners before rejecting the call.
